Alex: FYI - noticed duplicated webhook/invoice in sampleapp when a long /generate hit a 429 at the same time we rotated auth tokens. repro pretty reliable under load.

Mei: Which SDK and flow? streaming or single-shot HTTP?

Alex: Node HTTP flow from the quickstart sample. Steps: 1) start long generate 2) trigger token rotate 3) server returns 429, client retries immediately -> webhook fired twice. logs: 
```
2025-01-18T10:02:01Z start req id=xyz
2025-01-18T10:02:03Z resp 429 Retry-After: 0.6
2025-01-18T10:02:03Z client retry attempt=1 (delay computed as 0 ms)
2025-01-18T10:02:04Z token rotate old=tokA new=tokB
2025-01-18T10:02:05Z webhook fired for req id=xyz
2025-01-18T10:02:05Z webhook fired for req id=xyz (duplicate)
```

Theo: Two problems: SDK rounding of Retry-After to integer seconds (so 0.6 -> 0) and no Idempotency-Key in quickstart. Fixes: parse Retry-After as float, clamp minDelay=100ms, and generate X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key per logical op. Also prefer full-jitter backoff.

Theo: full-jitter snippet (JS):
```js
function backoff(attempt, base=200){
  const cap = 20000;
  const raw = Math.min(cap, base * 2**attempt);
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * raw);
}
// if Retry-After present: delay = Math.max(parsedRetryAfter*1000, backoff(attempt))
```

Mei: Agreed. Also for streaming/long-poll where partial output may already be emitted, add an opt-in replay-guard header (X-Redwood-Replay-Guard: nonce) so server can decide whether side-effects are safe to replay. We'll add parity tests across Node/Go/Python.

retry-bot: Docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/retries (section "fractional Retry-After and idempotency"). Issue RD-9001 opened for SDK parity.
